messages:
sara_sales: @rebecca_cust re: the Private POC — saw your note about the TLS failures when calling our private endpoint. can you paste the client-side error and which subnet the test VM is in?
rebecca_cust: getting this from our app when it calls /v1/generate -> "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". test VM is in private-subnet-3 (us-west-2a), no NAT.
eli_se: nagging question: is that VM supposed to reach the public CA/OCSP responder? if there's no NAT, it won't be able to fetch OCSP/CRL or any external cert chain resources. can you run: `openssl s_client -connect <private-endpoint-ip>:443 -showcerts` from the VM and paste output?
rebecca_cust: pasted minimal output: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 C = US, O = ExampleCorp, CN = private.redwood.example
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
verify return:1
```
we're using our corp CA, cert was issued by our int-ca.
mike_net: confirming what eli said — with no NAT gateway, instances in private subnets often can't reach external OCSP/CRL endpoints. also check if your Route53 private hosted zone is associated with the VPC — if it's not, the client might be resolving to a public endpoint or wrong IP. run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0123abcd` or just `dig +short api.redwood.private` on the VM.
rebecca_cust: dig returns 10.10.5.24 (that's our ENI-based endpoint). Route53 private zone is associated per our admin.
eli_se: ok. next suspicion: the TLS chain includes an intermediate which has an AuthorityInfoAccess OCSP URL pointing to `ocsp.our-ca.corp` and that hostname isn't resolvable from the private subnet (no DNS forwarder) or blocked by firewall. check `curl -v http://ocsp.our-ca.corp` from the VM.
rebecca_cust: `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: ocsp.our-ca.corp`
mike_net: that nails it — DNS for your internal CA OCSP responder isn't reachable. two options: (1) make sure the VM uses the VPC Resolver and that your internal DNS forwarders are reachable from that subnet, or (2) mirror the CA chain and install the root+intermediate into the VM trust store so OCSP isn't required.
oncall_infra_bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-83 assigned to mike_net. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-20260315-83
eli_se: quick workaround for the POC while network teams fix DNS: upload the CA bundle to the application container and configure the process to use `SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/ca-bundle.pem` so verify succeeds locally. not ideal long-term but gets the POC green.
sara_sales: RE: timeline — customer asked about pricing implications if we need a private peering/NAT. rebecca_cust can you confirm if enabling a small NAT gateway for egress is acceptable? that's the usual recommend and avoids modifying trust stores.
rebecca_cust: internal policy prefers to avoid NAT because of egress cost. would prefer internal DNS fix or trust bundle approach for POC.
mike_net: if avoiding NAT, we can create a VPC endpoint for the CA/OCSP hosts if they're hosted in a reachable AWS account, or configure the resolver to forward to your internal DNS servers via the VPC resolver endpoints. i'll validate permissions and firewall rules — likely need TCP/80 and TCP/443 egress to ocsp host and also allow resolver traffic (UDP/53).
eli_se: action items: (1) rebecca to provide CA bundle and test VM creds so we can push temporary bundle (2) mike_net to confirm DNS/egress firewall rules and whether VPC endpoint is feasible (3) sara to update the POC timeline & note potential NAT/endpoint cost. i'll provide a short script to install CA into the container: 
```
# inside container
mkdir -p /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/custom
cp /tmp/our-ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/custom/our-ca.crt
update-ca-certificates
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```
rebecca_cust: i uploaded our ca bundle to the shared S3 link you gave. testing now.
(10 minutes pass)
rebecca_cust: quick status — after adding CA bundle to container, TLS handshake works and requests succeed. sending perf tests. :tada:
eli_se: great. long-term we still prefer network fix. mike_net can you confirm whether there's an easy fix for DNS so that ocsp.our-ca.corp resolves from private-subnet-3?
mike_net: digging in — cause is DNS forwarder ACLs in the transit VPC. i'll open a firewall rule change request to allow VPC resolver to talk to corp-dns on UDP/53 and TCP/53, and allow outbound to ocsp.our-ca.corp IPs on TCP/80. estimated ETA EOD.
sara_sales: thanks all. i'll mark POC status as "workaround applied, awaiting infra fix" and update commercial team. rebecca, we'll waive any extra setup fees for the POC since this is network config.
rebecca_cust: appreciated. will retest after infra changes. thanks team. :pray:
deploybot: deploy hook: canary vpc-dns-fix patch scheduled to staging at 2026-03-15T20:30Z
eli_se: tagging this resolved for now — re-open if the infra change doesn't fully restore OCSP resolution.
rebecca_cust: confirm — after infra change (DNS ACL) all tests pass end-to-end. POC green. :white_check_mark:
